original_question: If G is a graph of maximum degree Delta, must its strong edge-chromatic number satisfy chi_s(G) <= 5 Delta^2 / 4 when Delta is even and chi_s(G) <= (5 Delta^2 - 2 Delta + 1) / 4 when Delta is odd? Equivalently, is the Erdos-Nesetril conjecture on strong edge coloring always true?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Conjecture 26: the Erdos-Nesetril conjecture on strong edge-coloring, with notation and the line-graph-square equivalence supplied by Section 1 and the opening paragraph of Section 4.1; it is also restated in abbreviated form as Open Problem 6 in Section 6. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct problem, uses the correct universal scope over graphs of maximum degree Delta, gives the exact parity-dependent upper bounds from the paper, and correctly names this as the Erdos-Nesetril conjecture. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
missing_details: The draft does not define chi_s(G) as the minimum number of colors in a strong edge-coloring. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

It leaves implicit what a strong edge-coloring is: two edges must receive distinct colors when they share an endpoint, or when they each share an endpoint with the same edge; equivalently, this is a proper coloring of the square of the line graph L(G). ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should explicitly say 'for every graph G with maximum degree Delta = Delta(G)' rather than relying on context. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
refined_question: Let G be a graph with maximum degree Delta = Delta(G). Is it true that the strong edge-chromatic number chi_s(G)—that is, the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of G such that any two edges receive distinct colors whenever they share an endpoint or whenever they each share an endpoint with the same edge—always satisfies chi_s(G) <= 5 Delta^2 / 4 when Delta is even, and chi_s(G) <= (5 Delta^2 - 2 Delta + 1) / 4 when Delta is odd? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since a strong edge-coloring of G is a proper coloring of the square of the line graph L(G), does chi(L(G)^2) always satisfy the same parity-dependent bound for every graph G of maximum degree Delta? ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))
justification: The nearest official formulation in the paper is Conjecture 26 in Section 4.1, not a broader neighboring problem. Your draft matches that conjecture essentially exactly. The paper defines strong edge-coloring in Section 1 and again at the start of Section 4.1, including the explicit equivalence with coloring L(G)^2, and Section 6 later lists the same problem more briefly as Open Problem 6 using the shorthand 1.25 Delta^2. Because your draft keeps the exact odd-Delta correction term, Conjecture 26 is the most paper-faithful target. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/ds25/pdf/))

citations.label: Definition of strong edge-coloring and strong edge-chromatic number
